cards.description:
As a player, I want to form or join an Alliance so that a larger group can play together, organize games, and manage shared Resources.

cards.title: Buying KIDUNA -- Tokenomics
cards.description:
As a member, I want a clear way to acquire and use KIDUNA so that I understand its value, purpose, cost, and consequences before making a purchase.

Done when the interface clearly explains the amount, exchange value, fees, intended uses, custody, and confirmation required for every transaction.

cards.title: Create tournaments and leaderboard
cards.description:
As a player, I want to join tournaments and see game results so that I can participate in organized competition and understand how the tournament is progressing.

Done when players can enter a tournament, follow its structure and results, and view a game-specific leaderboard that does not become a general measure of social worth.

cards.title: Voice chat through Gemini Voice API
cards.description:
As a player, I want to speak with the other participants during a game so that playing together feels immediate, social, and natural.

Done when players can deliberately join, mute, leave, and control voice chat, with clear indicators showing when voice is active.

cards.title: Implement the highest-priority feature
cards.description: Work on the most important feature slice first. Keep notes on the approach, any assumptions, and what still needs testing so the card is easy to review later.

cards.title: Fix the most visible bug
cards.description: Use this for the issue that most affects users or slows down the team. Keep the reproduction steps, root cause, and verification notes on the card while you work.

cards.title: Update tests and clean up edge cases
cards.description: Add or adjust tests while the code is still fresh. If the change touches multiple paths, note the cases that must be checked before moving the card forward.

cards.title: Invite & Onboarding
cards.description:
Very important – when you create an invite, you should be able to create a unique one for a single person or a general one you can always use

It should give you a URL and a QR Code for your general one

Also multiple special purpose ones – so if you’re going to a conference for example – and you want to give away $KIDUNA/Compute

When people register, they can already have STAKED $KIDUNA in their wallet – so they can’t sell it, but can use it.

As a new player, I want a short, welcoming introduction so that I can create my identity, understand the game, and begin playing without prior Kiduna knowledge.

Done when a new Source can join, create an Ally, learn the essential rules, receive free Chips, and enter or form a game.

cards.title: Desktop version
cards.description:
As a desktop player, I want a complete Royals and Rogues experience designed for a larger screen so that I can comfortably play, inspect cards, communicate, and manage the game.

Done when the current game works end to end on desktop and uses the latest Kiduna design system and quiet-enamel Royals and Rogues artwork.

cards.title: Review pull request
cards.description: Check the implementation against the acceptance criteria, verify test coverage, and leave clear feedback. Move the card on only after the review comments are resolved.

cards.title: Verify in staging
cards.description: Confirm the change behaves correctly in a realistic environment before calling it done. Check the main user flow, any related edge cases, and whether the fix introduced regressions.

cards.title: Ship and archive
cards.description: Once the work is approved and verified, mark it complete and archive the card. Keep this list as the final step so the board stays clean and current.
